destination.question: How do gauge fields, antisymmetric tensors or scalar-dependent curvature couplings change inflationary backgrounds and their consistency conditions?
destination.summary: These are distinct theory extensions with separate background, perturbation and stability questions.

systems: Single or triplet antisymmetric rank-2 fields
Brans–Dicke hybrid examples as a related scalar–gravity construction

conventions: Three two-form fields are not three scalar fields

excludes: Transferring scalar-only stability or slow-roll formulas unchanged
Inferring full stability from a background construction

sources.title: Anisotropic hyperbolic inflation

evidence.text: Integrate the Maxwell equation using conserved pA, then seek power laws α=ζ log t, σ=η log t, φ=ξ log t+φ0 and θ=γt^p+θ0 in the large-radius approximation.

sources.title: Inflation using a triplet of antisymmetric tensor fields

evidence.text: Use SVT decomposition, Fourier transformation, and quadratic perturbation actions to inspect kinetic coefficients. Solve the metric tensor equation through conformal-time rescaling, Bessel/Hankel functions, and subhorizon/superhorizon asymptotics.

sources.title: Scalar and vector modes in inflation with antisymmetric tensor field

evidence.text: Scalar-vector-tensor and Helmholtz decompositions separate metric perturbations and the electric/magnetic components of δB. Coordinate gauge transformations are derived, a gauge is fixed, and the action is expanded to quadratic order to obtain linear perturbation equations.

sources.title: Gauge-flation trajectories in Chromo-Natural Inflation

evidence.text: Numerically evaluate the approximate e-fold integral and compare it with integration of the full equations across the cases considered. Separately evolve the axion-integrated Gauge-flation action to compare phase-space trajectories with the full axion theory.

sources.title: Anisotropic hyperbolic inflation

evidence.text: Rewrite evolution as a dynamical system in Hubble-normalized variables using e-fold time. Classify fixed points, calculate Jacobian eigenvalues, and examine numerical trajectories and parameter flows.

evidence.text: Freeze radial motion, impose approximate phase-space balance in the dark-energy-dominated regime, and solve for a slowly moving radius at fixed θ. Check potential domination and compare the resulting trajectory with integrations.

sources.title: Cosmological dynamics of multifield dark energy

evidence.text: Compare phase-space evolution for normalized initial velocities spanning four orders of magnitude and for radial offsets βr_ini=−5,0,5. Larger initial velocities generate more pronounced oscillatory transients.

sources.title: Cosmological dynamics of multifield dark energy

evidence.text: Project the covariant Hessian normal to the trajectory, form the effective mass, and evaluate the reduced light-mode sound speed. The first normal-vector definition is usable; the extracted second equality needs clarification.

sources.title: Cosmological dynamics of multifield dark energy

evidence.text: Replace a slowly settling coordinate by its instantaneous force-balanced value, use its equation of motion to eliminate the remaining kinetic term, and evaluate the projected mass including field-space curvature. Here the eliminated kinetic variable is θ̇².
